criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The CHANGELOG entry and the doc comment on `plan::schema_reference_problem` both give the root cause: "the configuration files and the code that parses them (strict on unknown fields) are changed separately, and nothing connected a new section to the schema that must accept it before plan time". Both cite all three jobs.

criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core (run with `cargo test -p athena-core`) shows that a plan or change which modifies athena.toml without any crates/athena-data/ path is flagged with a message that names the schema file to change. The same test shows that a change that also modifies crates/athena-data/src/config.rs is accepted. The test fails on the base commit and passes with the change.
criteria.evidence: Three new tests passed in this snapshot: plan::tests::a_config_edit_without_the_schema_is_refused_and_with_it_accepted, reading::tests::a_reading_that_edits_configuration_without_the_schema_is_refused_at_plan_time and admission::tests::plan_admission_and_the_gate_agree_on_when_the_schema_judges_a_config_edit. They check that athena.toml alone, defaults.toml alone, a schema edit in the wrong crate (athena-core) and a deleted schema file are all refused, and that the refusal names crates/athena-data/src/config.rs or defaults.rs. They also check that athena.toml together with a modified crates/athena-data/src/config.rs is accepted. On the base commit the tests cannot compile, because the diff adds `schema_reference_problem`, `PlanEntry::schema_problem`, `MISSING_SCHEMA` and `config_edits_without_schema`, none of which exist on base. I did not check out base, because git state must not change.

criteria.criterion: The plan-time rule calls `athena_gate::defers_to_schema_test`/SCHEMA_DIR rather than duplicating the path, and a test confirms that the gate, admission and the plan rule agree on the same inputs (`cargo test`).
criteria.evidence: `schema_reference_problem` calls `athena_gate::config_edits_without_schema`, which calls `defers_to_schema_test`, and its message uses `athena_gate::SCHEMA_DIR`. findings.evidence: The diffstat shows 77 changed lines in reading.rs, which is not on the deliverables list. The change connects `schema_problem` to `reading::plan_entry`, the function production planning calls (athena-cli/src/drain.rs:1750). It also adds a test there. The reading itself was unsure where plan validation lives, and without this wiring the rule would never run. It is still outside the stated scope.

findings.summary: Any edit to athena.toml or defaults.toml is now refused at plan time, including a value-only edit, unless a crates/athena-data/ path is also listed
findings.evidence: Any non-deleted config path flags the plan when no schema path is listed. A plan that only changes an existing value must now list a schema file, for example crates/athena-data/tests/repo_config.rs. The reading accepted this rule and the CHANGELOG documents it as the narrowest sound form, but it can refuse plans that are fine.

summary: The change passes. It adds the requested plan-time rule. `athena_gate::config_edits_without_schema` is the other side of the existing `defers_to_schema_test` check and uses the same SCHEMA_DIR. `plan::schema_reference_problem` applies it through `reading::plan_entry`, so a plan that edits athena.toml or defaults.toml without a non-deleted crates/athena-data/ path is refused before production, and the refusal names config.rs or defaults.rs. The CHANGELOG and the doc comments name the root cause and cite all three jobs. I ran the new tests in crates/athena-core and crates/athena-gate and they pass in this snapshot. They cover config alone, the wrong crate, a deleted schema file, the accepted config-plus-schema case, and agreement between plan, admission and gate. They cannot compile on base, because the symbols they use are new; I judged that from the diff, not by running base. The existing deferral, unknown-field and repo_config tests also pass, and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs all passed. I found two minor issues: reading.rs changed outside the deliverables list (it is the wiring the rule needs), and the rule also refuses value-only config edits that list no schema path, which the reading accepted and the CHANGELOG documents.
